info.title: GEOly Data API
info.description:
Typed endpoints of the GEOly Data API (`x-geoly-stability: stable`): the account behind the key (GET /api/v1/quota, /api/v1/brand), the brand catalog (GET /api/v1/topics, /api/v1/prompts), monitoring records (GET /api/v1/prompts/{prompt_id}/records, /api/v1/records/{record_id}) and the incremental record feed (GET /api/v1/records), writes (POST /api/v1/prompts, POST /api/v1/prompts/{prompt_id}/runs) and windowed reports (POST /api/v1/reports/*). Authenticate with an API key bound to one brand; the brand is implied by the key and never appears in paths.

Stability: within /api/v1 the shape and meaning of every declared field is stable — fields are never removed, renamed or retyped, units never change, and enums only grow (response enums are open: ignore unknown values and unknown fields). Metric definitions follow the product and are recorded in the changelog. Breaking changes only ship under /api/v2.

Envelope: `{ data, page?, meta }`. `meta.quota` is the billing outcome of the call; `meta.schema_conformant` is false only if the report output drifted from this document (the data is still returned).

Pagination: send `limit` (and `cursor` from `page.next_cursor` for the next page, with exactly the same filters). `page.next_cursor === null` is the only end-of-list signal; `page.capped: true` means the position limit was reached before the end. GET /api/v1/prompts uses a true keyset cursor (ordered by created_at, id): a row whose sort key is unchanged and that still matches the filters is never skipped or repeated because other rows were added or archived meanwhile, and there is no position limit. It is not a snapshot: every page re-applies the filters, so a row archived before you reach it drops out of an active listing. `x-geoly-pagination` describes each list.

Errors use one envelope `{error:{code,message,details?},meta}`; `error.code` is drawn from the closed list in `x-geoly-error-codes`. Branch on the HTTP status and `error.code`, never on `message`. Stable keys of `error.details`: errors[] ({param, reason, allowed?, message}), reason, required, retry_after_seconds, max_bytes, actual_bytes, _quota, and resource / id (404 NOT_FOUND of a single-resource endpoint such as GET /api/v1/prompts/{prompt_id}).

Billing: each call is billed at the price in `x-geoly-cost` ({tier, base, unit, long_window_multiplier, guard_rpm}: nominal price per call in credits, the same as the matching GEOly MCP tool (GET /api/v1/records has none: it is offered only on this API, so its price and guard are its own), against the MCP credits pool; tier "free" with base 0 = not charged — this includes operations whose matching MCP tool is registered as not charged (charged:false: POST /api/v1/prompts and POST /api/v1/prompts/{prompt_id}/runs), so no nominal price is declared for them; guard_rpm is the per-organization requests-per-minute guard of that endpoint — counted per organization together with the same organization's calls of the matching GEOly MCP tool on the other surfaces (MCP, Agent API)). The billing outcome of every call is in `meta.quota`. A monitoring run still consumes monitoring credits, a separate pool, as described on that operation.

The HTTP tool wrappers under /api/v1/tools and /api/v1/tools/{tool} are retired: every method answers 410 TOOL_SURFACE_RETIRED, and for a known tool details.replacement names the resource endpoint. Use these resource endpoints. MCP and Agent API remain available.

x-geoly-error-codes.description: Request body is not a JSON object (or not valid JSON). Rejected before execution; not charged.

Arguments do not match the input schema (unknown parameter, wrong type, invalid enum value, missing required field), or an argument the tool could only reject after looking it up (unknown topic / country / platform code, malformed date window, ambiguous name …; details.reason carries the original tool code when there is one). Not charged: rejected before execution, or refunded.
The cursor is malformed or was issued for a different query. Drop it and start over.
Idempotency-Key header is present but malformed.

The request is valid but the current state does not allow it. details.reason says why: platform_not_enabled (the AI platform is not purchased for this brand) and locale_required (pass country + language; details.availableLocales lists them) are charged the minimum call fee under the current billing rule (meta.quota.charge = "min_fee"); a write conflict (name already taken …, details.reason = the original tool code) or an organization without brands is not charged. On the report endpoints, details.reason = request_rejected (the report rejected the arguments only after looking them up, e.g. "Brand not found", "No brand in scope.") is billed as the report settled — usually the full base price of the report; meta.quota.charge says which.
API key missing, invalid, revoked, expired, or its creator left the organization; on the tool surface also a credential that is not tied to a user (raised while the tool runs). Not charged.
The organization has no active subscription (checked at authentication, or by the tool for the organization that owns the referenced resource). Not charged.
MCP credits used up for this period. Retry after the quota resets, or upgrade.
The organization's plan does not include this tool.
A plan limit (brands, prompts …) is reached. Upgrade or free a slot.
The credential is not an API key bound to a brand (legacy org tokens and OAuth tokens are not served here).
The credential spans several organizations and none was selected.
The credential has no accessible organization.

The credential is not permitted to do this: denied at authentication (non-API-key credentials; details.reason carries the original reason), a resource read/write permission the key was not granted, or an id outside this key's brand / organization. Not charged.
Unknown report name in POST /api/v1/reports/{report}; see the API reference for the list. Not charged.

The referenced id / name does not exist for this brand. Billing depends on how the tool reports it (see meta.quota.charge): a not-found returned in the tool result keeps the tool's own settlement, receipt also in error.details._quota — the call-priced prompt and record detail reads (POST /api/v1/reports/prompt-overview, GET /api/v1/records/{record_id}) are charged as one call ("charged"), audit detail and search-query filters the minimum call fee ("min_fee"); a not-found raised while the tool runs (topic_name, brand_id …) is refunded ("refunded"); one rejected while resolving the scope (before execution) is not charged ("unbilled"); free tools and free endpoints report "free".
HTTP method not supported on this path; see the Allow header.
The Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request body.
A request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running. Retry with the same key after Retry-After.

The outcome of this write, or of an earlier attempt with the same Idempotency-Key, cannot be determined: it may have been applied in part or in full. error.message carries the tool message when there is one. Check the resource with a GET before retrying; with a key, retry only with a new key.

The HTTP tool wrappers under /api/v1/tools and /api/v1/tools/{tool} are retired. Answered for every method before authentication; nothing runs and nothing is charged. For a known tool details.replacement names the resource endpoint: one replacement object, or an array of them for a tool with several views or several replacements. Every replacement object has method and path and may carry when (the old arguments it replaces, for example {view: "table"} or {section: "board"}) and note (marks a replacement that is not drop-in). details.openapi points to this specification.
Request body exceeds 64 KB.
Request body must be application/json.
The query would scan too much data. Narrow the window / filters.
The serialized response exceeds the 4 MB limit for one API response (details.max_bytes / details.actual_bytes). Lower page_size / limit or narrow the filters. Decided before settlement; not charged.
Per-credential requests-per-minute limit. Honor Retry-After.
Per-tool rate guard on a heavy query. Honor Retry-After.
Too many concurrent tool calls for this credential / organization. Honor Retry-After.
Organization hourly database-seconds budget exhausted. Honor Retry-After; pace with X-DB-Budget-*.
Unexpected server error. Retry once with backoff; report the Request-Id if it persists.
The call hit its time limit (error.details / error.message carry narrowing hints). Not charged.
The data layer is overloaded. Not charged; retry later.
The tool is temporarily disabled after repeated failures. Not charged; honor Retry-After.
A read failed and the call was refunded (charge "refunded", occasionally "refund_pending"; the receipt is in error.details._quota). Not charged; retry later.

The record feed is not ready: its dedicated index is missing or invalid, or the database role cannot see all in-flight transactions to place a safe watermark. No fallback table scan is performed and no checkpoint advances.

The persistent claim could not be acquired. No write was executed, and retrying with the same key never executes twice. If the failed claim could not be cleaned up, the retry answers REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS for up to 5 minutes and then IDEMPOTENCY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; in that case check with a GET and use a new key.

get.summary: Incremental completed records and subsequent changes
get.description: Completed records ordered by changed_at then id, not by record date, so a late completion appears at its completion update. Uses a dedicated index and a safe watermark at least five minutes behind database time; a long-running database transaction that has already written holds the watermark at five minutes before its start until it ends, and polls in that time return nothing newer but are still billed. Scan work is bounded, so an empty page can have next_cursor. Follow next_cursor until it is null, then save page.sync_cursor and poll with it; every 5 to 15 minutes is enough, because nothing newer than the watermark is returned. Bound the first sync with updated_since rather than business_date_from, which filters inside each scanned batch and does not shorten the scan. With a cursor, updated_since is ignored; keep limit, business_date_from and include unchanged. Repeated records are updates: upsert by id. Analysis fields are read-time values: mention_rank backfills do not advance changed_at, so a rank change alone is not re-emitted. Deletions and records that leave completed are not emitted either. Reconcile by starting a separate pass without a cursor from an updated_since rewound at least 24 hours (a rewound updated_since sent together with a saved cursor is ignored and reconciles nothing), or by re-reading records by record date. Optional answer_text and citations expansions; citations cap at 30 with a flag. Every call, including an empty poll, is billed at the price in x-geoly-cost.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: Initial inclusive lower bound on changed_at for the first page (UTC with milliseconds). Ignored when cursor is present.

parameters.name: business_date_from
parameters.description: Optional earliest business day; filters inside each scanned batch and does not shorten the scan (UTC+8 business day, YYYY-MM-DD).

post.description: Creates a prompt under the API key brand. Returns 201 and Location. Optional Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate execution; successful results replay for 24 hours. Unknown write outcomes are never automatically retried. tags_state reports whether every requested tag was read back (saved), some were not saved (partial) or the saved tags could not be confirmed (unavailable); tags_warning explains anything but saved. The prompt exists in all three cases.

get.description: The prompt list straight from the prompt table: text, country, status, topic, tags, timestamps and whether the text names the brand — no metrics (use POST /api/v1/reports/prompts for per-prompt visibility). Ordered by (created_at, id) ascending with a true keyset cursor: a row whose (created_at, id) stays the same and that still matches the filters is never skipped or repeated because others were added or archived meanwhile; there is no snapshot — a row archived before you reach it drops out of an active listing, and new rows appear at the end. Follow page.next_cursor until it is null; page.total counts every matching row. Free (no credits); no metrics are computed. Guarded at 200 requests per minute per organization: one bucket for GET /api/v1/prompts, GET /api/v1/prompts/{prompt_id} and the same organization's get_prompt_list view=catalog calls on the GEOly MCP / Agent API — separate from the prompts report's bucket.

get.description: Paginated records, including pending and failed runs. At most 10,000 positions per query are reachable (page.capped); narrow the date window to continue. Cursors bind the brand, prompt, filters and limit. Pagination is not a snapshot: concurrent changes may skip or repeat records. Use explicit dates and deduplicate by id. Windows over 90 days use the long-window multiplier in x-geoly-cost. Billed per call at the price in x-geoly-cost, using the existing MCP credit meter. Billing outcomes are in meta.quota.

bearerAuth.description: API key from Settings → Developer → API keys (prefix geom_). Each key is bound to one brand.

Request-Id.description: Unique id of this request (equals meta.request_id). Include it when reporting a problem.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed per credential in the current one-minute window. Sent on every response after the API key has been authenticated; absent on errors raised while authenticating (401) and on 405.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the current window resets (0–60).

X-DB-Budget-Limit.description: Organization database-seconds budget per rolling 60 minutes. Sent on every response after authentication.

X-DB-Budget-Used.description: Database seconds used by the organization in the last 60 minutes.

X-DB-Budget-Reset.description: Seconds until the oldest usage bucket expires.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (429; 503 when retryable).

Allow.description: Methods supported on this path (405 responses).

changed_at.description: Update position of this record (prompt_record.updated_at, microseconds). The feed orders by changed_at then id; upsert by id.

mention_rank.description: Read-time value. Rank backfills do not advance changed_at, so this can change while changed_at stays the same and the feed will not re-emit the record for it. To reconcile, poll again from an updated_since rewound by an overlap of at least 24 hours, or re-read records by record date.

citations.description: Requested with include=citations: up to 30 per record, ordered by position (nulls last) then id — the same order and cut as GET /api/v1/records/{record_id}. citations_truncated flags a cut.

The prompt exists in all three cases: never create it again because of this field. Known values: "saved", "partial", "unavailable"; more may be added.

tags_warning.description: Why tags_state is not saved; null when it is saved.

FeedPage.description: Bounded incremental scan. Empty pages can have a continuation. Persist sync_cursor after processing data; do not advance on schema_conformant=false.

next_cursor.description: Continue this scan: pass as `cursor` with the same limit, business_date_from and include (updated_since is ignored with a cursor). null = caught up to the watermark.

sync_cursor.description: Checkpoint to persist together with the processed rows. After next_cursor is null, poll later with it (every 5 to 15 minutes is enough). null only when schema_conformant is false: do not advance.

watermark_at.description: Exclusive upper bound of this scan: at least five minutes behind database time and never past the oldest in-flight transaction.

CursorPage.description: Cursor pagination. next_cursor === null is the only end-of-list signal.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` with the same filters and limit to get the next page.

capped.description: Present when the position limit was reached before the end of the list.

KeysetPage.description: Keyset pagination (ordered by created_at, id). next_cursor === null is the only end-of-list signal; there is no position limit, so `capped` never appears.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` with the same filters and limit to get the next page.

total.description: Total rows matching the filters (not just this page).

TopNPage.description: Top-N report: only `limit`; next_cursor is always null.

report.description: Report name for POST /api/v1/reports/{report}; resource labels include quota, brand, topics, prompt-catalog, prompt, prompt-records, prompt-records-latest, record, record-feed, created-prompt and prompt-run.

schema_conformant.description: true = data matches the documented schema exactly (every declared key present). false = the report output drifted; data is still returned as mapped (or null) — treat it as best effort.

QuotaMeta.description: Billing outcome of this call. remaining / resets_at / unlimited are null on paths that never reserved credits (free reports, calls rejected before execution) — except QUOTA_EXCEEDED, which carries the live balance. Absent when the call was rejected before the report ran (schema errors, cursor errors, authentication).

cost.description: Credits actually charged for this call.

remaining.description: Credits left this period; null when unlimited or unknown on this path.

charge.description: [Extensible enum] charged = normal settlement (per row, or one call for a call-priced read — including a not-found from the prompt or record detail); min_fee = minimum call fee (no data / not found from a per-row report / platform not purchased / missing locale); free = free report or endpoint; refunded / refund_pending = failed and refunded; unbilled = rejected before execution, or not metered.

details.description: Stable keys: errors[] ({param, reason, allowed?, message}) on INVALID_ARGUMENT; reason; required (PERMISSION_DENIED); retry_after_seconds (429); max_bytes / actual_bytes (413 / 422); _quota (receipt); resource / id (404 NOT_FOUND of a single-resource endpoint). Other keys are informational and may change.
